newsitem.title: USA: Heska gets animal flea bite allergy patent.
newsitem.headline: Heska gets animal flea bite allergy patent.

text.p: Heska Corp said Friday it got a patent covering a method to extract the allergens causing flea bite allergy in animals.
The company said it developed and a test to detect flea bite allergy in dogs using the allergens covered by the patent. It added it is optimizing a similar test for cats.
The animal health product company said flea bite allergy is one of the most common skin diseases afflicting dogs and cats.
The company said the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office granted the patent, which is named "Ectroparasite saliva proteins and apparatus to collect such proteins."
Heska went public at $8.50 a share July 1 after lead underwriter Credit Suisse First Boston had cut the offering price from $10. The company had initially proposed a price of $14 to $16.
Heska's stock traded at 9-3/8 Friday morning, up 5/8 and a new high since the July 1 offering.
